A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM-based robust unlearning study. The text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original WMDP and MUSE experiments, relearning and jailbreaking evaluations, loss-landscape analyses and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds a LLaMA-3 8B comparison reporting unlearning performance, attack robustness and runtime.

M1.justification: The SAM-enhanced unlearning procedure, smoothing variants, objectives in Equations (1)–(12), and Algorithm A1 are retained. Added model evaluations and perturbation percentages do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use WMDP Bio, MUSE Books/News, Wikitext retention data, MMLU utility evaluation and AGNews/GSM8K/SST2 relearning data. The added LLaMA-3 evaluation changes model configuration within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v4 newly evaluates TAR and RMU-LAT in Table 1; v3 only discussed their source papers. This substantially extends the comparator set to external defenses designed for attack resistance. Existing NPO, GradDiff, RMU and smoothing-variant comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v4 adds a LLaMA-3 8B evaluation using 60 relearning samples for one epoch, with runtime as an additional metric. Existing Zephyr and MUSE settings remain. The landscape-loss description also changes from cross-entropy to a sign-inconsistent log-probability formula; this does not establish that the plots were recomputed.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds a focused computational-efficiency analysis relating runtime to robustness against relearning. Existing loss-landscape, attack-strength, data-source, RMU-layer, perturbation-radius, token-KL and generation-example analyses are retained. Relocating the radius-sensitivity summary does not introduce another ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions state that attack performance is averaged over five independent random trials. Existing uncertainty displays are retained, with no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: v4 adds results for one LLaMA-3 attack setting: post-attack UE is 0.70 for NPO+SAM and TAR, 0.41 for NPO and 0.44 for RMU-LAT; reported runtimes are respectively 11.5, 7441.9, 5.8 and 10.3 minutes. These are new-setting results. v3 Table 1 survives as v4 Table 2 with unchanged values, and appendix scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The SAM derivations and assumptions remain unchanged. However, Section 4 replaces the cross-entropy description with an explicit mean log-probability definition for the landscape loss. As printed, it lacks the negative sign needed for equivalence and conflicts with the retained higher-loss-means-better-unlearning interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: connecting robust unlearning to SAM, extending this perspective to other smoothing techniques, and improving resistance to relearning and jailbreaking.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new comparison as favoring weight perturbations over activation perturbations and SAM's efficiency over TAR's meta-learning overhead. Its new Impact Statement identifies risks of erasing essential knowledge and obstructing later recovery. Naming 'shallow unlearning alignment' largely restates an existing explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly quantifies the existing RMU perturbation ranges as 2.43% and 5.68% of parameters and removes the explicit 32-layer total. Table 1 adds runtimes. Appendix C hyperparameters and code-access information are retained, without corresponding detailed implementation or timing information for the new comparison.

R1.justification: Related-work citations are pruned, including Challenging Forgets, Vaccine, Lo et al.'s relearning paper and diffusion-unlearning studies. Section 5.2 adds focused positioning against already-cited TAR and RMU-LAT through efficiency and perturbation-space comparisons. The main novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the order of Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–F remain intact. Local changes include the new comparison discussion and Impact Statement, revised shallow-alignment terminology, relocation of the radius-sensitivity summary, and conference and affiliation text.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper in the main text and references, extensively reflowing equations and repositioning or resizing figures and tables. Figure 4 now uses surrounding text, Figure 2(c) is redrawn, and a new Table 1 precedes the retained table, renumbered Table 2.

improvement.justification: The new LLaMA-3 comparison against TAR and RMU-LAT addresses v3's lack of empirical comparisons to these robust defenses and exposes a useful runtime–utility trade-off. This provides a limited net gain, tempered by missing implementation and timing details and the newly sign-inconsistent landscape-loss formula. The existing method, principal results and ablations remain substantially intact.
